caveat: Public X sample only. Not geotagged. A state name in the text is not proof the poster is there. Chips are themes, not word counts. Click a chip for the brief.

glossary.fare: Lagos / SW public-transport fare increases after subsidy reform and FX pass-through. Used as a shorthand for cost-of-living anger aimed at the centre and at Sanwo-Olu.
glossary.Lagos: Commercial capital and Tinubu's political home. High volume of national political talk is written as if it were local.
glossary.hardship: Catch-all for inflation, naira weakness, fuel price and food costs after the 2023-24 reforms. Dominates citizen talk more than security in many southern feeds.
glossary.2027: Next presidential cycle. Posts treat current performance as a referendum on a second term rather than on today's policy.
glossary.home-base: South-West as Tinubu's electoral core. Support is assumed, not enthusiastic; criticism is framed as disappointment from his people.
glossary.thin: Little sustained X talk about the NSA / ONSA in that area. Security office is not the main character in the local feed.
glossary.economy-first: Security posts lose to pocketbook posts. NSA is mentioned, if at all, after fuel, food and fares.
glossary.second-term: Explicit argument for or against Tinubu running again in 2027. Often bundled with elite horse-trading, not street polling.
glossary.Kano-vehicles: Federal vehicle / empowerment gifts into Kano and the North-West, read locally as 2027 mobilisation rather than service delivery.
glossary.Arewa: Northern political identity frame. Used both by supporters and critics.
glossary.bandits: Armed groups running kidnap-for-ransom and village raids across the North-West, especially Zamfara, Katsina, Kaduna, Sokoto.
glossary.Fulani: Ethnic label used in X security talk — sometimes as herder identity, often as a slur attached to bandit or farmer-herder violence. Treat as a discourse marker, not an order-of-battle.
glossary.Ribadu: Nuhu Ribadu, National Security Adviser. Personal brand is stronger than the ONSA institution in most posts.
glossary.mixed: No single story wins the feed. Security, living costs and local governors share the thread.
glossary.insurgency: North-East jihadist war (JAS / ISWAP and splinters). Older than this administration; still the NE security frame.
glossary.Zulum: Babagana Umara Zulum, APC governor of Borno. Often praised independently of the President; used as a competence contrast.
glossary.Boko-Haram: Colloquial label on X for NE jihadists. In the field it splits into JAS (Shekau line) and ISWAP. Posts rarely make that split.
glossary.Borno: Epicentre state for the NE insurgency and for IDP / reconstruction talk.
glossary.ONSA: Office of the National Security Adviser — the institution around Ribadu. Mentioned less than the man.
glossary.kidnap: Abduction for ransom on highways, in schools and in rural NW / NC communities. The crime type most often laid at the NSA's door.
glossary.farmer-herder: Communal / resource conflict in the Middle Belt, especially Benue and Plateau. Distinct from NW banditry; X often collapses the two.
glossary.highways: Kaduna-Abuja and other trunk roads as kidnap and ambush ground. Travel risk is how many users experience insecurity.
glossary.abduction: Same family as kidnap; used when the victim set is students, clergy or aid staff rather than a routine roadside tax.
glossary.rejected: South-East frame that Tinubu has no popular mandate there. 2023 voting pattern plus sit-at-home politics.
glossary.Obi: Peter Obi. Still the reference opposition figure in SE / urban youth talk, even out of office.
glossary.sit-at-home: IPO-linked Monday shutdowns in the South-East. Economic pain and a running test of state authority.
glossary.gunmen: SE / SS label for unidentified armed groups — secessionist, criminal, or both. Vague on purpose in local reporting.
glossary.unpopular: South-South reading of Tinubu: oil-producing states that do not treat him as their candidate and measure him on derivation and security of assets.
glossary.oil: Crude production, theft, host-community bargains and the fiscal lifeline of the federation. SS political weather.
glossary.oil-crime: Pipeline vandalism, illegal refining and associated militia / cult economies in the Delta.
glossary.Sanwo-Olu: Babajide Sanwo-Olu, APC governor of Lagos. Takes first-line blame for fares, traffic and state taxes; Tinubu is the backdrop.
glossary.cash-cow: Charge that Lagos is taxed as a federal ATM while services lag. Aimed at both the governor and the President's Lagos network.
glossary.must-go: Protest slogan for the President or a governor to leave office. High heat, low organisation on X.
glossary.not-the-story: NSA / ONSA barely appears in that state's X sample. Living costs or the governor crowd it out.
glossary.emilokan: Yoruba 'it is my turn'. Tinubu's 2023 succession slogan; now used in Ogun / SW as both loyalty badge and taunt.
glossary.reciprocity: SW argument that the zone delivered 2023 and is owed federal attention, projects or 2027 discipline.
glossary.2027-vehicles: Same as Kano-vehicles: asset gifts read as early campaign logistics in Kano.
glossary.Abba: Abba Yusuf, NNPP governor of Kano. Local politics (Ganduje / Kwankwaso / Yusuf) often outranks the President in Kano threads.
glossary.El-Rufai: Nasir El-Rufai, former Kaduna governor, now a loud critic of Tinubu and of Ribadu's appointment. His posts still set NW elite weather.
glossary.NW: North-West geopolitical zone — bandit belt plus large APC / opposition swing weight.
glossary.JAS: Jama'at Ahl al-Sunna lid-Da'wa wal-Jihad — Shekau-line Boko Haram. Still active in parts of Borno / islands of the Lake Chad basin.
glossary.ISWAP: Islamic State West Africa Province. The more coherent NE jihadist force; competes with and has largely overtaken JAS in many sectors.
glossary.herders: Armed or armed-adjacent pastoral groups in Benue / Plateau talk. Overlaps with farmer-herder; not the same as NW bandit gangs.
glossary.killings: Plateau / Middle Belt mass-casualty attacks. Communal and criminal violence that X treats as a single failure of the centre.
glossary.communal: Identity-linked rural violence (ethnic / religious / land) rather than a named franchise like ISWAP or a bandit kingpin.
glossary.Fubara: Siminalayi Fubara, PDP governor of Rivers. Locked in a power struggle with his predecessor; national presidency is read through that fight.
glossary.Wike: Nyesom Wike, FCT minister, former Rivers governor. The other pole of the Rivers crisis and a Tinubu ally.
glossary.oil-theft: Organised crude theft in Rivers and the wider Delta. Security and revenue problem; NSA is expected to coordinate the response.
glossary.Aso-Rock: Presidential villa / the centre. FCT talk often means the Presidency rather than Abuja municipal issues.
glossary.absence: Charge that the President is missing from a crisis — travel, silence, or no visible visit — used as a legitimacy attack.
